title: The Rigveda Khilani
textType: Hymns in verse outside the received recension
attributionNote: The hymns that stand outside the received Śākala recension of the Ṛgveda and were transmitted beside it: the appendices on the marriage and funeral rites, the Kuntāpa hymns, the Āprī and other additions. GRETIL's e-text follows J. Scheftelowitz, Die Apokryphen des Rgveda (Khilani), Breslau 1906, and was input by Muneo Tokunaga.
description: The Khilāni are the Ṛgveda's own supplements: the verses recited over the wedding and the funeral, the Kuntāpa songs of the sacrificial ground, the Śrī hymns to fortune and the additions on the metre and the divine ordering of the sacrifice. They are hymns the Vedic ritual needed and the school recension did not carry, and they were recovered from the ritual sutras and the manuscripts that preserve them.
historicalContext: Vedic ritual books quote verses as Ṛgvedic that the received text does not contain; Scheftelowitz collected them from the Vedic ritual and ancillary literature, which is why the collection stands in the corpus as the outer edge of the Ṛgveda rather than as a school recension.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: the 584 verses of the Khilāni, divided into book and hymn, streamed from GRETIL at read time. A second, shorter series of marks the same file carries for the appendix of the appendix is not published as a division of the work and no markers of that series are indexed.
